summary: Jinbo Shi is a scholar of history, archaeology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Minzu University of China and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences under Jingru Wang. He held posts at CASS, Minzu University, Ningxia University, and North Minzu University.
Jinchuan Wan is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Wan held professor positions at both National Central University and Fo Guang University, attested in 2010.
Jing Yin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti. Yin served as Director at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2006–2010).

Jing-shen Tao is a sinologist and historian who studied at National Taiwan University and Indiana University Bloomington (Ph.D. circa 1963–1967). Tao served as Professor of East Asian Studies at the University of Arizona (~1976–2003) and Correspondence Research Fellow at Academia Sinica.
Jingru Wang (1903–1990) was a scholar of linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Tsinghua University from circa 1928 to 1932 and held a post at Minzu University of China circa 1953.
Jingyi Yang works in Indology, Tibetology, and computational studies. Yang studied at the University of Hamburg and served there as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin, attested in 2026.

Jinhua Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed graduate studies at McMaster University and postdoctoral research under Noritoshi Aramaki at Kyoto University. His career includes posts at the University of Virginia and the University of British Columbia (attested 2008–2018).

Jinhua Jia is a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied under Yunji Chen and Paul W. Kroll at the University of Colorado Boulder (PhD 1994–1999). Jia held posts at CU Boulder, Hong Kong Polytechnic University, and the University of Macau.
Jinling He is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Hiroki Okumura.
Jinping Liao is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.

Jinshi Fan is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Peking University under Su Bai. She served as Director of the Dunhuang Academy from 1984 to 2014 and held a post at Lanzhou University.

Jinzhang Peng (1937–2017) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He served at Wuhan University (~1963–1986) and held positions as dean of the archaeological institute and researcher (professor) at Dunhuang Academy (~1986–2017).
Jiro Abe was a Japanese philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1904–1907). He held academic posts at Japan Women's University (~1913–1923) and Tohoku University (~1923–1945).

Jiro Kawakita was a scholar of Tibetology who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1939 to 1943. He held posts at the Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1960–1977), University of Tsukuba (~1977–1985), and Chubu University (~1985–1993).

Jiro Murata was a scholar of history, archaeology, and sinology who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1917 to 1920. He held a post at the National Institute of Technology, Akashi College, from circa 1963 to 1969.

Jiro Sugiyama (1928–2011) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1953). He held posts at Tokyo National Museum, Nagaoka University of Technology, International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and Bukkyo University.
Jiryo Masuda was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Unrai Wogihara. Masuda served as a professor at the University of Calcutta.
Jishu Oda was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as Rector at Choboji Monastery (attested 1914) and held a professor emeritus post at Shuchiin University (attested 1977).

Jitendra Nath Banerjea was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and religious studies. He studied under Hemchandra Raychaudhuri and served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta from circa 1918 to 1959.

Jitendra Nath Mohanty was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, and University of Göttingen. He taught at Calcutta, Burdwan, The New School, and Oklahoma, and served as professor at Temple University (~1986–2012).
